stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Apple is implementing new restrictions on 'full disk access' for Macs.
The change is a direct response to security risks associated with advanced AI agents.
The update aims to ensure users must intentionally grant this high level of application access.

stories.title: Apple changes full-disk access permissions to curb abuse from AI agents
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Apple is modifying full-disk access permissions to restrict potential misuse by AI agents.
The change addresses concerns regarding AI agents reading private user messages.
The article highlights a disagreement between Apple and Meta regarding the adequacy of existing regulatory frameworks (like the FDA) to prevent this abuse.

stories.title: US arrests tech CEO accused of smuggling $300M in Nvidia chips into China
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A tech CEO has been arrested in the US for allegedly smuggling $300 million worth of Nvidia chips into China.
The incident highlights ongoing and persistent challenges related to the export control and smuggling of advanced semiconductor technology.
This case underscores the geopolitical tensions surrounding high-end AI hardware and US export restrictions to China.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown

The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon through Ollama 0.31.
The speed improvement is achieved via Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher quality outputs, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: An OpenAI safety employee has quit and is sounding the alarm
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: A former OpenAI safety employee, David Robinson, has resigned from his role.
Robinson is now publicly raising concerns about the safety aspects of OpenAI's major model releases.
His warnings are being shared through an editorial published in The Atlantic.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck in real-time animation of 3D Gaussian avatars, which typically requires costly neural inference.
Proposes GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation), a distillation method that approximates complex animations using a linear combination of identity-independent blendshapes.
Replaces heavy per-frame neural decoding with a much lighter shallow coefficient predictor for faster, real-time performance.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: Introduces KaliBench, a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM evaluations by moving beyond knowledge-based tests to measure practical, syntax-sensitive command generation.
Features 'runtime-free verifiable rewards,' suggesting a novel approach to automated, reliable evaluation of tool-use capabilities.

stories.title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
stories.author: Kaiming He
bullet_points: Introduces VISTA, a visual harness designed to unlock reasoning potential in multimodal AI models.
VISTA provides general-purpose multimodal models with long-horizon vision capabilities.
The system maintains a lossless visual memory, allowing the model to actively retrieve past environmental observations.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck in real-time animation of 3D Gaussian avatars, which typically requires costly neural inference.
Proposes GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation), a distillation method to approximate complex animations using linear combinations of blendshapes.
Replaces per-frame heavy neural decoding with a much faster, shallow coefficient predictor for efficient avatar animation.

stories.title: The Missing Primitive: Diagnosing and Repairing Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
stories.author: Zhengzhong Tu
bullet_points: The research addresses the fundamental question of whether LLMs possess true structural mathematical understanding, not just pattern matching.
It introduces the concept of 'Mathematical Primitive' as a new diagnostic tool to probe the underlying reasoning capabilities of LLMs.
The study aims to use these diagnostic findings to systematically improve the post-training and mathematical reasoning abilities of large language models.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: Introduces KaliBench, a new fine-grained benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM evaluations, which often focus on knowledge or high-level agentic tasks rather than precise CLI command generation.
The benchmark emphasizes verifiable rewards without requiring full runtime execution, focusing on the accuracy of command syntax and tool invocation.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
Decision models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon devices.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Meta open sources code to let you make Muse AI gadgets
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Meta has open-sourced the code for its Muse AI agent.
This allows users to build custom 'Muse gadgets' integrating the AI.
Suggested applications include displaying Muse on E Ink screens or HDMI sticks.

stories.title: Netflix is pivoting away from prestige
stories.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
bullet_points: Netflix is reportedly changing its content strategy by moving away from high-profile, prestige productions.
The shift is evidenced by the termination or winding down of multiyear production deals with established directors.
This strategic pivot is being observed in contrast to rival streaming services.

stories.title: OpenAI’s Dot agent is enterprise software that can also order your dinner
stories.author: Allison Johnson
bullet_points: OpenAI has introduced a new agent platform named 'Dots'.
The platform is positioned as enterprise software, capable of performing various tasks, including ordering food.
The article contrasts Dots with Meta's Muse, noting Dots' more 'workplace' feel.

stories.title: Rivian’s sales pop as the company’s big R2 bet starts to pay off
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Rivian reported significant Q3 growth, with production increasing 85% year-over-year.
Vehicle deliveries saw a substantial 45% jump in the third quarter.
The positive sales trend suggests the company's strategy, including the upcoming R2 model, is gaining traction.

stories.title: Amazon’s $1B plan to combat data center backlash draws more backlash
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Amazon is facing criticism despite efforts to address data center privacy concerns (e.g., ending NDAs).
The primary backlash centers on Amazon downplaying the environmental impact and pollution from its data centers.
The story highlights the ongoing tension between corporate tech expansion and environmental/social accountability.

stories.title: Lyft settles landmark driver misclassification lawsuit for $272.5M
stories.author: Cyrus Farivar
bullet_points: Lyft has settled a significant lawsuit regarding the misclassification of its drivers.
The settlement amount reached $272.5 million.
The resolution faces criticism from groups claiming drivers are still owed substantial compensation.

stories.title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: Introduces RPG, a framework for autonomous self-improvement of embodied robot agents.
The system improves robot execution capabilities without requiring updates to the underlying model weights.
RPG uses offline data to identify skills and generates simulation tasks for practice using execution feedback.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduces ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to test the ability of AI to retrieve inspiring prior research papers.
The benchmark leverages human expertise by using researchers to annotate which past works were crucial to their own projects.
Addresses a key gap in current AI research: the ability to identify novel connections and inspirations within vast scientific literature.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: SILSA introduces a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation using compact sliding-window slice latents.
It addresses limitations in existing methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) which fragment surfaces and weaken topological consistency.
The framework aims to improve topological preservation and reduce generation costs for complex 3D shapes.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models as an alternative to discrete autoregressive models.
Addresses a key limitation of discrete diffusion models: independent token sampling during parallel decoding.
Proposes using a shared continuous state for denoising to maintain statistical dependencies among decoded tokens.

stories.title: DMAD: Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation for Fast Visual Generation
stories.author: Chongyang Ma
bullet_points: Introduces DMAD (Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation) to improve fast visual generation.
DMAD recasts distribution matching into a classification problem to learn log-density ratios directly.
It aims to overcome the high memory and computation costs associated with auxiliary diffusion models in previous methods.

stories.title: Higher-Order Molecular Grammars for Generative and Foundation Models in Chemistry
stories.author: Tolga Birdal
bullet_points: Introduces Higher-order Grammar Representation (HGR) to address limitations in molecular learning models.
HGR is designed to explicitly encode complex chemical topologies, such as ring systems and recurring motifs, which standard formalisms struggle with.
The framework aims to be a principled, topology-aware alternative to existing, often computationally demanding, higher-order representations.

stories.title: Embedding Prediction Helps Image Generation
stories.author: Stella X. Yu
bullet_points: The research proposes using predicted embeddings as a conditioning mechanism in diffusion transformers for image generation.
The core technique involves training a Next-Embedding Predictive Autoregression (NEPA) model to forecast sequential embeddings.
This approach leverages the relationship between noisy and clean image embeddings during the denoising process.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: SILSA introduces a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation using compact sliding-window slice latents.
It addresses limitations in current methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) where surface fragmentation and topological inconsistency occur.
The core innovation aims to maintain topological consistency while reducing generation costs compared to existing fragmented token approaches.

stories.title: TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: TACO is a new optimizer designed to reduce the memory overhead associated with full-parameter fine-tuning of Large Language Models (LLMs).
It addresses the memory limitations imposed by large LLMs on modern GPUs, a significant bottleneck in current LLM deployment.
TACO offers an alternative to existing state compression or gradient modification techniques, aiming to improve efficiency without sacrificing performance relative to AdamW.

stories.title: Cost-augmented Schrödinger bridges on graphs are exactly solvable: a Feynman-Kac tilt replaces learned control
stories.author: Akshay Balsubramani
bullet_points: The research addresses the problem of finding a generalized Schrödinger bridge on graphs that incorporates a state-visitation cost.
A key finding is that the cost-augmented bridge can be solved exactly by employing a Feynman-Kac tilt on the reference process.
This exact solution eliminates the need for complex learned control mechanisms and temporal-difference penalties previously used in approximation methods.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models (CDLMs) as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
CDLMs aim to overcome the independence bottleneck in discrete models, where parallel decoding severs token statistical dependencies.
The core mechanism involves denoising a shared continuous state, which is the key innovation presented.

stories.title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of step-size selection in large-scale LLM fine-tuning optimization.
Introduces Zero-and-First-Order optimization (ZFO) to decouple direction selection from step-size.
ZFO uses a first-order optimizer for direction and zeroth-order evaluations along a 1D subspace for step-size selection.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduces ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to test the ability of AI to find inspiring prior research.
The benchmark leverages expert human knowledge, using researchers to annotate which past papers influenced their own work.
Addresses the challenge of AI systems needing to sense relevant, often buried, prior ideas within massive research archives.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
Addresses a key limitation of discrete diffusion models: independent token sampling during parallel decoding, which breaks statistical dependencies.
Continuous diffusion models mitigate this by denoising a shared continuous state, allowing for better modeling of token relationships.

stories.title: Every Ablation Is a Dose: Counterweights and the Semblance of Self-Repair
stories.author: Vinay Kumar Sankarapu
bullet_points: The paper investigates the phenomenon of 'self-repair' in language models, where components compensate when others are removed (ablated).
Previous studies suggested self-repair is noisy and lacks a single clear mechanism.
The authors propose a unifying hypothesis: self-repair is an emergent property stemming from pre-existing gains within the model architecture.

stories.title: AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
stories.author: Xin Dong
bullet_points: Introduces AutoCompact, a method to train coding agents to intelligently manage context in long-horizon software engineering tasks.
Addresses the challenge that early context in long coding trajectories becomes stale, requiring agents to decide when and how to compact state.
The agent learns a policy to determine what working state to preserve and how to resume tasks after context compression.

stories.title: Keyword Harnesses Fail Open: A Cheap Diagnostic Ladder for Tool-Use Claims in Small Language Models
stories.author: Juan S. Santillana
bullet_points: Keyword-matching benchmarks can incorrectly validate tool-use capabilities in small language models (false positives).
The paper proposes a 'cheap diagnostic ladder' to rigorously test and validate actual tool-use in LLMs.
The study demonstrates that models with different training regimens can score identically on lenient metrics, highlighting evaluation flaws.

stories.title: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think
stories.author: Yilun Du
bullet_points: The paper investigates new methods for enhancing frontier models beyond standard Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL).
It challenges the conventional view that RL is superior for generalization while SFT suffers from weak generalization and catastrophic forgetting.
The proposed 'Finetuning with Sampling' method explores leveraging off-policy expert data, a strength of SFT, to improve model capabilities.

stories.title: Argo-Bench: Evaluating Data Agents on Enterprise-Scale Workflows
stories.author: Joseph J Ma
bullet_points: Argo-Bench introduces a new evaluation framework for data agents designed for complex, enterprise-scale workflows.
It addresses the limitations of existing text-to-SQL benchmarks, which only test query generation and often have flawed answer keys.
The framework uses public datasets to simulate real-world scenarios requiring reasoning across multiple tables and statistical analysis.

stories.title: Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes
stories.author: Spyros Gidaris
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'Where-OPD,' a method applying on-policy self-distillation to Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
This technique aims to improve MLLM reasoning by using a student model supervised by a privileged version of itself.
It addresses a gap in current MLLM research, which often limits visual information use to simple image crops for fine-grained perception.

stories.title: Show HN: Offrun – manage every coding agent from one workspace
stories.author: arunbhatia
bullet_points: Introduces 'Offrun,' a workspace designed to manage multiple coding AI agents simultaneously.
Supports integration with various models, including Claude Code, Codex, AGY, and Grok Build.
Provides centralized oversight to track agent activity, dependencies, and resource usage.

stories.title: I got targeted: Trying to get your credentials via a git post-checkout hook
stories.author: frankwiles.com by frankwiles
bullet_points: The article discusses a security vulnerability where credentials can be targeted via a Git post-checkout hook.
This highlights a specific, practical security risk within developer workflows.
It serves as a cautionary tale regarding the security implications of Git hooks.

stories.title: gVisor is being donated to CNCF
stories.author: gvisor.dev via carlana
bullet_points: gVisor, a container runtime security technology, is being donated to the CNCF.
This move integrates gVisor into the Cloud Native Computing Foundation ecosystem.
The donation signifies increased industry adoption and standardization for container security.

stories.title: The More Context You Give Your AI Coding Agent, the Worse It Can Get
stories.author: robertadam987_
bullet_points: Challenges the common advice to always provide extensive context to AI coding agents.
Suggests that over-contextualization can lead to degraded or worse AI performance.
Highlights a nuanced operational issue in the practical application of AI development tools.

stories.title: 🛑 Stop Writing Code Like It's 2026: How I Built an Autonomous Agent Pipeline That Actually Works
stories.author: hizba_cloud
bullet_points: Focuses on the shift towards autonomous agent pipelines as a major software engineering innovation.
Suggests that the current focus on new JavaScript frameworks is less significant than agent-based development.
Presents a practical, hands-on case study of building a functional autonomous agent pipeline.
